clue.text: Attempt to get one's own way with nasty trinket first

definitions.text: Attempt to get one's own way

indicators.note: first says the trinket word is placed ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a charm is a small trinket worn on a bracelet
nasty means offensive

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win an argument by first producing an unpleasant little ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the trinket ahead of the nasty word, though the clue mentions it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign of flattery and friendliness designed to win people over is an attempt to get one's own way.

clue.text: A Poet Laureate appearing in outstanding feature on 'Sir Bruce Forsyth — Comedy Great'

indicators.note: appearing in means set inside the other piece

parts.note: the entertainer Bruce Forsyth was famous for his jutting chin
PL is an abbreviation for Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A TV tribute to Bruce Forsyth, the veteran British entertainer, includes a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce Forsyth was a long-running British TV host famous for his jutting jaw; 'appearing in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin is one of the greatest figures of silent film comedy.

clue.text: Champion hit with mysterious torpor capturing hearts for appearing human

indicators.note: capturing means holding the other piece within
mysterious suggests something obscure and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A champion, struck by a strange lethargy, loses heart and looks merely human.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAMPION and TORPOR are scrambled together, signalled by 'mysterious', with H taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropomorphic describes something given human form or traits, so seeming like a person.

clue.text: Old lady joining church club

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, or ma
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An elderly woman joins her parish society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society to join, but it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked or flanged head.

clue.text: The Spanish grumble about lacking resolve

indicators.note: about means turned around, and here it turns each piece where it stands

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to beef is to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: Spaniards complaining about a lack of determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns both pieces: EL becomes LE and BEEF becomes FEEB, giving FEEB + LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means weak, so lacking strength of will or resolve.

clue.text: This is Wedding Ale so sup boisterously

indicators.note: boisterously suggests rowdy, disordered behaviour, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Guests are told to drink the wedding beer noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is' links the definition to the wordplay; ALE SO SUP is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal is a formal word for marriage, or the ceremony of a wedding.

clue.text: Photo with women's clothing on is a plant

parts.note: a snap is a snapshot, or photo
drag is women's clothing worn by a man

explanation.surface: A snapshot shows a man in a dress, revealing he is a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a plant' suggests an undercover agent, but the plant is the garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, antirrhinum, is a garden plant with flowers that open like a mouth.

clue.text: Significant numbers consumed by Page 3?

definitions.meaning: vital means significant and statistics are numbers, read literally
the measurements of a topless model, eagerly devoured by readers of the Sun's Page 3

explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of the Sun, a British tabloid, featured topless models, whose bust, waist and hip measurements are what readers devour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means important data such as births and deaths, and jokingly a woman's measurements.

clue.text: Y-reg Seat half rebuilt in spring

indicators.note: rebuilt suggests the parts reassembled in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the hyphen dropped

indicators.note: half picks the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: An old Spanish car, half rebuilt, sits beside a hot spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-reg was a British number-plate prefix from 2001; SEAT is the Spanish car maker. 'half' gives SE; 'rebuilt' rearranges YREG and SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically erupts with water and steam.

clue.text: Teleprompter showing report of traffic jam

indicators.note: report of says the words are heard spoken rather than read on the page

parts.note: a traffic jam is a queue of autos, or cars

explanation.surface: A newsreader's prompting screen is showing the latest bulletin on road congestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' signals that 'auto queue' is said aloud, giving the sound of the trade name.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocue is the British trade name for a teleprompter, the screen that shows a presenter their script.

clue.text: Soft toy rabbit

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
a rattle is a baby's toy

explanation.surface: A cuddly plaything shaped like a bunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like the cuddly toy, but it is the British slang verb for chattering on, so it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit (on) is to talk at length about trivia, the same as to prattle.

clue.text: Metallic thread not unknown in angler's fly

indicators.note: not says the following piece is taken away from the thread's name

parts.note: Lurex is a yarn woven with metallic thread
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: Fishing flies tied with glittering thread.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the unknown X from LUREX.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is an artificial bait, such as a fly, used to attract fish.

clue.text: 11 fields unexpectedly in bloom

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out in a jumbled, surprising way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the number points back to the answer to 11 across, a lure

explanation.surface: A surprising flowering appears across the meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' scrambles LURE (the answer to 11) with FIELDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lis is the stylised iris flower of French heraldry, so a bloom.

clue.text: Education Secretary claims new team working to make progress

indicators.note: claims means takes hold of, so the other piece sits inside

parts.note: Michael Gove was Britain's Education Secretary at the time

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: on means working, as of a machine

explanation.surface: The minister lays claim to a newly assembled team that is busy pushing reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove held the post when this puzzle ran; 'new' rearranges the team, which 'claims' puts inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a move on is an idiom meaning to hurry up, so make progress quickly.

clue.text: Revolutionary check involving two pawns to create pincer

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the built word is read from the end back
involving means taking the other piece within it

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
P is the chess abbreviation for a pawn, so two give PP

explanation.surface: A chess player puts the king in check using a pair of pawns, forming a pincer movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' builds REPPIN, which 'Revolutionary' then turns backwards; a nipper is a claw, not a child, here.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipper is an informal word for a pincer or claw, as on a crab.

clue.text: Tobacco tin with flower on the side

parts.note: a tin is a can
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A tin of tobacco decorated with a flower on its side.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaster is a coarse dried tobacco, originally sold in rush baskets.

clue.text: Relief from tension for one in daze over plan backfiring

indicators.note: over means above, so in this down clue the first part sits on top
in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: backfiring means going the wrong way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart

explanation.surface: A dazed person, whose plan went wrong, looks for some way to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' looks like an example signal, but 'one' gives the letter; 'backfiring' turns the plan into PAM, which 'over' sets below in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Diazepam, better known as Valium, is a drug that relieves anxiety and muscle tension.

clue.text: Nothing missing from note I bash out for the missus

indicators.note: missing from says the zero is removed from the note

parts.note: a memo is a written note
O, shaped like zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost nothing writes a note and then lashes out at their wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O from MEMO to get MEM; 'out' rearranges I BASH into SAHIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Memsahib was the Indian term for a married European woman, and is used jokingly for one's wife.

clue.text: Teaching of Wise Men derived from periodical practice

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, or periodical
an ism is a distinctive practice or doctrine

explanation.surface: The wisdom of sages is said to come from reading a magazine regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Magism is the doctrine of the Magi, the priestly wise men of ancient Persia.

clue.text: Dumpling gained weight

parts.note: won means gained, as a prize
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Eating dumplings, someone put on pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonton is a Chinese dumpling of seasoned meat in thin dough, often served in soup.

clue.text: Strait formed by two rivers on the edge of Oxfordshire engaged in swan-upping

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside the other piece
upping means raised up, so in this down clue the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, so two give RR

indicators.note: the edge of picks the first letter of the county name

explanation.surface: A narrow channel is created by two rivers in Oxfordshire during the annual swan count on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: Swan-upping is the annual census of swans on the River Thames. RR and O go inside NAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrows is a narrow stretch of water between two larger bodies, so a strait.

clue.text: Cavils about Eastern European

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Petty objections are raised about someone from the eastern part of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavic describes the Slavs, the peoples of eastern Europe such as Russians and Poles.

clue.text: French novelist second to go on about limits of ripening cheese

indicators.note: second to says the novelist comes after the other part
about means placed around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written, the two words joined

indicators.note: limits of picks the outer letters at each end of the word

parts.note: Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A writer from France ranks second after a rambling talk on ripening cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps GO ON round the edges of 'ripening' to make GORGON, the snake-haired monster, a red herring of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue-veined Italian cheese named after a town near Milan.

clue.text: Some insurrectionists arraigned despot

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several rebels have been charged in court by an autocratic ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the absolute ruler of Russia, so the word is used for any autocrat.

clue.text: Brother down south seen now and again in Burberry

indicators.note: now and again means every other letter of the brand name is picked

explanation.surface: A brother from the American South is spotted occasionally wearing a Burberry coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Burberry is a British fashion house known for raincoats.
explanation.definitionFit: Brer is a Southern US dialect form of brother, as in the Brer Rabbit tales.

clue.text: Difficult journey with Blatter taking in Switzerland against Luxembourg

indicators.note: taking in means holding the other pieces within

parts.note: Sepp Blatter was the president of FIFA, world football's governing body

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the two codes sit side by side

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: FIFA's boss faces a hard trip as Switzerland plays Luxembourg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' signals the insertion; the surface pictures a football match because Blatter ran FIFA.
explanation.definitionFit: A schlep(p) is a tedious or arduous journey, from Yiddish.

clue.text: Nice green I go in dizzy attack

parts.note: in Nice, a French city, green is vert
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a green on the Riviera, someone makes a giddy charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, not the adjective, so its green is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of spinning giddiness, so a dizzy spell.

clue.text: Company engaged in dodgy coins crime is getting what it deserves?

indicators.note: engaged in means set inside the other letters
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm involved in counterfeiting money finally receives its comeuppance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' puts CO inside ECONOMICCR, the rearrangement of COINS CRIME signalled by 'dodgy'; IS stays as printed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark admits the stretch: a financial slump is pictured as the economy getting its comeuppance.
